matched.failure: A handler calls engine.HandleContext(c) after rewriting the URL. c is put in the pool. A second request calling pool.Get() receives the same *Context while the first request's chain still uses it. The later Put from ServeHTTP then adds it a second time, so two concurrent requests can share Keys, Params and Writer.

matched.title: reset in HandleContext wipes state and replaces the outer handler chain
matched.failure: A middleware sets Keys (for example a user id) and a handler calls HandleContext. After it returns, the outer chain's remaining handlers see Keys nil and a different c.handlers and c.index. Handlers can be skipped or run twice, and post-Next logging or auth code loses its data.
notes: severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading did not confirm the failing case (Re-entering a rewritten request needs a reset and a fresh handler chain, and that is what the feature is for. After the inner run the index is at the end, so the outer chain stops, which is the expected result of a soft rewrite.)
